title: Graded Nakayama for a connected graded algebra
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $A=\bigoplus_{a\geq0}A_a$ be an internal direct sum of $k$-subspaces of a commutative unital $k$-algebra, with $A_aA_c\subseteq A_{a+c}$ and $A_0=k\cdot1$ via the structure map. Set $I=A_+=\bigoplus_{a>0}A_a$. Let $M=\bigoplus_{b\in\mathbf Z}M_b$ be an internally graded $A$-module with $A_aM_b\subseteq M_{a+b}$, finitely generated as an ungraded $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. (1) If a finite family of homogeneous elements $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ has images spanning the $k$-vector space $M/IM$, then $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ generate $M$ as an $A$-module. (2) If $IM=M$, then $M=0$. The empty generating family and the zero module are allowed; no Noetherian or finite-type hypothesis on $A$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0EKB (lemma-graded-NAK), parts (4) and (1), specialized to the displayed connected graded algebra; see also section-graded for the conventions.

proof.text: The subspace $I$ is an ideal: multiplying any positive-degree component by a nonnegative-degree component still has positive degree. Choose finite ungraded generators of $M$ using [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Replace each by its finitely many homogeneous components. These components still generate, since their span contains every original generator. Thus choose homogeneous generators $y_1,\ldots,y_s$, with $y_i\in M_{d_i}$. If $s=0$, then $M=0$.

source.place: Tag 0EKB (lemma-graded-NAK), proof of (1) and reduction of (4) to (1); section-graded for internal grading and quotient conventions.

proof.text: First suppose $IM=M$. For $s>0$ choose $j$ with $d_j=\min_i d_i$. Since $y_j\in IM$ and the $y_i$ generate, there are $a_i\in I$ with $y_j=\sum_i a_i y_i$: expand each module factor in an expression for $y_j\in IM$ in the generators, and collect coefficients (which remain in the ideal $I$). Write $a_i=\sum_{t>0}(a_i)_t$ using the internal grading of $A$. Every summand $(a_i)_t y_i$ lies in $M_{t+d_i}$, where $t+d_i>d_j$. Projecting the equality to $M_{d_j}$ therefore gives $y_j=0$.

source.place: Tag 0EKB (lemma-graded-NAK), proof of (1) and reduction of (4) to (1); section-graded for internal grading and quotient conventions.

proof.text: Remove this zero generator. The remaining homogeneous family still generates $M$, and $IM=M$ is unchanged. Induction on the number $s$ now proves $M=0$: the base $s=0$ was checked in step 1, and step 2 reduces every positive $s$ to $s-1$. This proves clause (2) for every module satisfying the displayed hypotheses.

source.place: Tag 0EKB (lemma-graded-NAK), proof of (1) and reduction of (4) to (1); section-graded for internal grading and quotient conventions.

proof.text: For clause (1) put $Q=\sum_{i=1}^r Ax_i$. This submodule is graded: in an expression $q=\sum_i a_i x_i$, decompose each $a_i$ into homogeneous components; the degree-$b$ component is $q_b=\sum_i(a_i)_{b-\deg x_i}x_i\in Q$, with negative coefficient degrees interpreted as zero. Let $N=M/Q$ and let $N_b$ be the image of $M_b$. These pieces span $N$. They are independent: if $\sum_b m_b\in Q$ with $m_b\in M_b$, the component calculation gives $m_b\in Q$ for each $b$. Thus $N=\bigoplus_b N_b$ internally, with $A_aN_b\subseteq N_{a+b}$. The images of the finite generators of $M$ generate $N$, so $N$ is finite.

source.place: Tag 0EKB (lemma-graded-NAK), proof of (1) and reduction of (4) to (1); section-graded for internal grading and quotient conventions.

proof.text: The spanning hypothesis modulo $IM$ says that for every $m\in M$ there are $c_i\in k$ with $m-\sum_i c_i x_i\in IM$. Since $\sum_i c_ix_i\in Q$, it follows that $M=Q+IM$. Under $M\to N$, the image of $IM$ is exactly $IN$: both consist of finite sums of positive-ideal scalars times images of module elements. Hence $IN=N$. Apply clause (2), proved in steps 1--3, to the finite internally graded module $N$ of step 4 to obtain $N=0$. Therefore $Q=M$, proving clause (1). The argument includes $r=0$, $M=0$, and $A=k$; it never uses Noetherianity or finite type of $A$.

lean.statement: theorem nakayama_connected {k : Type u} [Field k] {A : Type v} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] (𝒜 : ℕ → Submodule k A) [GradedAlgebra 𝒜] (hzero : 𝒜 0 = LinearMap.range (Algebra.linearMap k A)) {M : Type w} [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module k M] [IsScalarTower k A M] [Module.Finite A M] (ℳ : ℤ → AddSubgroup M) (hℳ : DirectSum.IsInternal ℳ) (hsmul : ∀ (a : ℕ) (b : ℤ) (f : A) (m : M), f ∈ 𝒜 a → m ∈ ℳ b → f • m ∈ ℳ ((a : ℤ) + b)) : (∀ (r : ℕ) (x : Fin r → M), (∀ i : Fin r, SetLike.IsHomogeneousElem ℳ (x i)) → Submodule.span k (Set.range (fun i : Fin r ↦ ((HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant 𝒜).toIdeal • (⊤ : Submodule A M)).mkQ (x i))) = ⊤ → Submodule.span A (Set.range x) = ⊤) ∧ ((HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant 𝒜).toIdeal • (⊤ : Submodule A M) = ⊤ → Subsingleton M)
